The ergative alignment does not apply generally to main clauses (which instead follow a nominative-accusative or split-intransitive pattern); rather, it is conditioned by a subordinate context. In aspectual categories akin to the imperfective, such as the inchoative aspect expressed by a subordinating particle, the agentive argument (A) of a transitive verb requires ergative marking.

The presence of ergative alignment in the perfective/completive aspect is conditioned by the syntax of subordination (relative, complement, and temporal-aspectual adverbial clauses). When the subordinate clause expresses a perfective or completive action, the transitive argument A obligatorily adopts the ergative case marker (te/ket), while the main independent clauses in perfective employ the unmarked nominative pattern in the free pronoun.

Split ergativity occurs with respect to past tense. In independent main clauses in the past tense, the subjects of both transitive and intransitive verbs follow a nominative alignment, using free pronouns. However, if the past-tense clause is subordinate (such as a relative or adverbial clause), the ergative marker (-te for 1st/2nd person or -ket for 3rd person) is mandatory for the transitive argument A.

Non-past tense (present and irrealis/future) in independent main clauses follows a nominative pattern, with no case marking on free pronouns. However, since ergativity is conditioned by the syntactic subordination environment, subordinate transitive clauses in the present or future/irrealis tense (relative, inchoative, comparative, or adverbial) obligatorily show ergative marking (te for 1st and 2nd person; ket / kət for 3rd person).

The indicative mood corresponds to the syntactic domain of realis (introduced by the declarative particle na). In simple main clauses in the indicative, free pronouns follow a nominative alignment without case marking. However, when a proposition in the indicative mood contains a subordinate transitive clause, the agent argument A obligatorily requires the ergative postpositions (te / ket).

Ergative alignment in marking occurs in non-indicative and irrealis moods when transitive clauses are subordinated or integrated into complex constructions (such as conditional, optative, or relative clauses in the irrealis).
